Because the passport, banking and intelligence claims are the substance of the event, they should remain attributed allegations rather than statements of established fact. A reliable account needs independent reporting or primary records that establish what Maxwell did, when it happened and whether the alleged KGB connection is supported.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Kushner Omits 100+ Foreign Contacts on Security Clearance Form SF-86
proposal.original_synopsis: In May 2017, it was revealed that Jared Kushner had filed an initial SF-86 security clearance application that omitted more than 100 foreign contacts, including meetings with Russian Ambassador Sergey Kislyak and the head of a Russian state bank under U.S. sanctions. Kushner's lawyers characterized the omissions as an accident caused by submitting the form prematurely, but career security officials viewed the incomplete disclosure as disqualifying. The form was amended multiple times as additional contacts came to light. The sheer volume of omissions — more than a hundred foreign contacts — stretched credulity that the errors were innocent, particularly given that many of the omitted contacts had direct bearing on the FBI's counterintelligence investigation.

frozen_original.title: Trump Pardons Dennis Hastert Ally With Alleged Donor Connection
frozen_original.synopsis: In January 2019, Trump granted clemency to a man with alleged connections to disgraced former House Speaker Dennis Hastert, who had been convicted of federal crimes related to covering up historic child sexual abuse. The pardon raised questions about the criteria for Trump's clemency decisions and whether donations or political connections played a role. Trump's pardon record across his first term showed a consistent pattern of clemency flowing to political allies, campaign donors, people with shared social networks, and those who had received advocacy from Trump confidants—rather than being driven by traditional Justice Department clemency review processes. Former officials noted that Trump had effectively privatized the pardon power, making it responsive to personal loyalty and social relationships rather than established legal standards.
